name: daydeck-mcp
description: Read and edit your Daydeck wallpaper plan — projects, phases, and rhythms.
long_description: Daydeck is a macOS wallpaper that shows a calm macro timeline: one lane per project, a few big blocks ("Project • phase"), recurring rhythms, and ongoing bars. It is not a task manager. This extension lets Claude read the current plan, add or edit projects and blocks, and check the plan for pacing problems (overloaded days, blocks touching weekends, blocks that run too long or too short, and more) — all against the same data.json Daydeck itself reads and writes.

tools.name: get_plan
tools.description: Read today's date and every project with its tasks, optionally expanded into a day-by-day view.

tools.name: add_project
tools.description: Create a new project (lane); refuses duplicate names.

tools.name: add_block
tools.description: Add a fixed, ongoing, weekly, or monthly task to a project; creates the project if needed.

tools.name: update_block
tools.description: Edit an existing task by id, including switching its kind.

tools.name: remove_project
tools.description: Delete a project and all of its tasks.

tools.name: set_project_status
tools.description: Set a project to active, draft, or off.

tools.name: check_pacing
tools.description: Check the plan for pacing problems and get concrete suggestions.

prompts.name: daydeck_weekly_planning
prompts.description: Run a weekly planning conversation: review what changed, propose moves, apply them, and check pacing.
prompts.text: You're running a weekly planning check-in for Daydeck, a calm macro timeline (NOT a task manager — no micro tasks, just a few big blocks per project). 1. Ask what changed since last week: new projects, finished phases, shifted deadlines. 2. Call get_plan (days: 14) to see the current plan and what's already on each day. 3. Propose concrete moves: new blocks, phase splits, status changes — always as "Project • phase" from a start date to an end date (or ongoing/weekly/monthly). 4. Apply the agreed changes with add_block / update_block / remove_block / set_project_status. 5. Run check_pacing (days: 14) and walk through any violations with the suggested fix. 6. Summarise in two short lists: "what I feel good about this week" and "what I don't".
